finding_info.title: AI agent account reading an application-specific password store
finding_info.desc:
An AI agent account read a store that holds an application-specific password (ASP) - a mail client's saved credentials (.msmtprc, .mbsyncrc/.isyncrc, .offlineimaprc, .muttrc/.neomuttrc, .fetchmailrc, Thunderbird's logins.json), an Emacs/Gnus .authinfo(.gpg), a .netrc/_netrc machine entry, or a git-credentials store. This is the host-observable slice of MITRE T1697 Steal Application Specific Passwords (new in ATT&CK v20): ASPs are secondary passwords a user generates to let a legacy app or non-interactive tool into an account, and because they sidestep interactive MFA, a stolen ASP lets an attacker reuse the account while bypassing MFA.
Be honest about scope: T1697 is mostly an identity-provider / SaaS technique - generating an ASP at the IdP, phishing a user for one, then logging in over a legacy non-MFA path - and that is invisible to a host EDR (it lives in IdP/SaaS audit logs, which is what the technique's own analytics key on). What banken CAN see is the one host-adjacent variant the technique lists, "obtain an ASP stored on a system": the agent reading an on-host ASP store. That is what this rule catches, scoped by account so it is clean signal from an agent that has no business reading another identity's mail credentials.
credential_file_read owns the host-wide SSH-key / shadow / cloud-secret reads (and overlaps on .netrc and .git-credentials); this is the account-scoped, application-specific-password framing and adds the mail-client / .authinfo stores that the host-wide rule does not carry. This is an "agentic AI detection" rule. See rules/agent/README.md.
